observation_summary: The bug report and failing test indicate that FastDateFormat ignores the timezone set on a Calendar object when formatting the 'z' (timezone name) pattern, instead using the system default timezone. This is a regression where the implementation logic for retrieving the timezone name was changed to use a cached value rather than the dynamic value from the Calendar instance.
hypothesis: The TimeZoneNameRule class in FastDatePrinter incorrectly uses a cached TimeZone instance (initialized at rule creation) instead of dynamically retrieving the TimeZone from the Calendar object passed to the appendTo method during formatting.
prediction: The TimeZoneNameRule.appendTo method will be found to use a stored TimeZone field instead of calling calendar.getTimeZone().
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly identifies the root cause as the removal of forced timezone handling and the subsequent failure of TimeZoneNameRule to respect the Calendar's timezone. The fix involves changing the rule to dynamically query the Calendar object for its timezone, which is a procedural/algorithmic correction in how the timezone name is determined.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a failure to correctly implement the formatting logic for the 'z' pattern. The code was changed to use a static/cached timezone instead of the dynamic one provided by the input Calendar, which is a procedural error in the formatting algorithm.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a field is initialized, the core issue is the logic of the appendTo method which fails to use the correct dynamic source for the timezone.
There is no missing guard or predicate; the logic simply uses the wrong data source for the formatting operation.
